description: We are MBA Robotics, a student team passionate about robotics, coding, and space exploration. For NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to build a prototype to help astronauts monitor their health, sleep, activity, and emotional well-being on long missions. We welcome teammates interested in programming, data analysis, UI/UX design, health research, and presentations. Join us to learn, create, and solve challenges together!
summary: Astronaut Health Panel is an interactive self-assessment tool built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge on health monitoring software. On long missions, astronauts carry much of the responsibility for spotting health changes in themselves. In our tool, the user takes the astronaut’s role: they complete a self-report, take a short Cognition-style attention and memory battery, enter vital signs, symptoms and routine checks, and see the results on a color-coded panel. The panel shows each indicator together with its data quality, maps the health risks that NASA’s Human Research Program links to the five spaceflight hazards, explains what the app can and cannot measure, suggests actions, and refers serious findings to the flight surgeon. Students and space enthusiasts can explore how health monitoring could work on a station, a rover, or a Moon/Mars base. It is an educational prototype and does not diagnose.
